newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Australian bonds weighed down by U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Australian bonds weighed down by U.S. data.

text.p: *Australian bonds pull back sharply from last week's records
as Treasuries sold off on signs of a stronger U.S. economy.
*Bonds expected to gain some support from local fundamentals
and rate outlook if U.S. continues to weaken.
*Trading seen subdued due to NSW bank holiday.
Australian bonds pulled back sharply from last week's record levels as U.S. market concerns about the strength of the economy saw 30-year Treasuries drop two full basis points.

Bonds were off sharply in SYCOM -- the 10-year contract dropped 15.5 points and the three year was off 10 points -- although the local market was expected to find support from the positive fundmaentals that led to last week's rate cut. There is also speculation there could be another cut in the pipeline.
Accordingly, spreads to Treasuries could narrow last week as the local market outperforms in a bearish market, analysts said.

While Treasuries were able to deal with a stronger than expected U.S payrolls report -- with stronger payrolls and a fall in the unemployment rate balanced by steady average hourly earnings -- the market was startled by a 2-1/2 year high reading on the National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) Index.
Trading on Monday was expected to be affected by the bank holiday in New South Wales.

While not a full market holiday, many were taking the day off. This week's key release is Thursday's July labour force report, which is expected to show the labour market remains stagnant, and keep talk of a further rate cut alive.
